question.problem:
If
    $U=[\begin{aligned}-v & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]$
and
$\text{det}(U)=4$, what is the value of $v?$
question.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(U) & =|\begin{aligned}-v & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-v\cdot 3-5\cdot 4 \\  & =-3v-20\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(U)=4$, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(U) & =4 \\ -3v-20 & =4 \\ -3v & =4+20 \\ -3v & =24 \\ v & =-8\end{aligned}
$$
